critical-current-test: Critical current tests are short-circuit tests additional to the basic test-duties of [[iec-56]] 6.106, applicable only to circuit-breakers whose critical current is below 10% of the rated short-circuit breaking current — the case if average arcing time in Test-duty No. 1 is significantly greater than in Test-duty No. 2 ([[iec-56]] 6.107.1). The critical current is the current, well below rated, that yields the longest arcing time and thus the most onerous thermal duty on the interrupter. Tests are made at currents of 4%-6% and 2%-3% of rated short-circuit breaking current ([[iec-56]] 6.107.2). The duties follow Test-duty No. 1 ([[test-duty]]), but the [[transient-recovery-voltage]] time t3 is modified by the factor sqrt(10/X), X being the test current as a percentage of rated. Small inductive currents are covered separately by [[magnetizing-and-small-inductive-current-switching-test]].
single-phase-short-circuit-test: Single-phase short-circuit tests are additional to the basic short-circuit duties of [[iec-56]] 6.106 and apply only to three-pole breakers for earthed-neutral systems having the three poles in one enclosure, or three separately-enclosed poles coupled mechanically with a common opening release ([[iec-56]] 6.108.1). The test demonstrates that operation is not adversely affected by the unbalanced electromagnetic forces produced when only one pole carries current. It must be shown that the breaker can break its rated short-circuit breaking current — d.c. component not exceeding 20% — through one pole only, with the [[transient-recovery-voltage]] from Tables IIA-IIX divided by the first-pole-to-clear factor and a power-frequency recovery voltage of U/sqrt(3) ([[iec-56]] 6.108.2). The [[test-duty]] is a single breaking operation, applied through an outer pole, or the pole giving maximum stress on the inter-pole coupling ([[iec-56]] 6.108.3).
short-line-fault-test: Short-line fault tests are short-circuit tests additional to [[iec-56]] 6.106, applying only to three-pole breakers for direct connection to overhead lines, rated 52 kV and above with rated short-circuit breaking current exceeding 12.5 kA ([[iec-56]] 6.109.1). They are onerous because a fault a short distance down the line imposes a steep, sawtooth (approximately triangular) [[transient-recovery-voltage]] on the line side — the line-side oscillation reaching peak ui in time ti — superimposed on the source-side recovery, severely stressing the gap just after current zero. Source impedance corresponds to about 100% rated current; two line impedances reduce the a.c. component to 90% and 75% ([[iec-56]] 6.109.2). The single-phase circuit combines supply and line-side components ([[iec-56]] 6.109.3-6.109.4). The [[test-duty]] comprises opening-only operating sequences at (90 plus/minus 5)% and (75 plus/minus 5)% with the appropriate prospective TRV ([[iec-56]] 6.109.5). See [[short-line-fault]].
out-of-phase-test: Out-of-phase making and breaking tests are required only if a [[rated-out-of-phase-breaking-current]] has been specified ([[iec-56]] 6.110.1). They verify the breaker can make and break under out-of-phase (loss-of-synchronism) conditions, which are onerous because the recovery voltage across the gap approaches twice the system voltage. The test-circuit power factor must not exceed 0.15, with roughly half the applied and recovery voltage on each side ([[iec-56]] 6.110.2). Applied and power-frequency recovery voltage equal 2.0/sqrt(3) (earthed-neutral) or 2.5/sqrt(3) (other systems) times rated voltage; [[transient-recovery-voltage]] follows 4.106 ([[iec-56]] 6.110.3). Two [[test-duty]] series (Table XVIII): Test-duty No. 1 at 20-40% and No. 2 at 100-110% of rated out-of-phase breaking current, opening-operation d.c. component below 20% ([[iec-56]] 6.110.4). Test-duty No. 1 may be omitted where [[critical-current-test]] is not required.
capacitive-current-switching-test: Capacitive current switching tests apply to all breakers assigned a rated line-charging, cable-charging, single- or back-to-back capacitor-bank breaking current, or capacitor-bank inrush making current ([[iec-56]] 6.111.1). They verify [[restrike]]-free performance when interrupting the small capacitive charging currents of lines, cables and capacitor banks; the duty is onerous because, after current zero, the trapped charge leaves up to twice the peak voltage across the gap, and any restrike causes severe overvoltages. Line-charging below 72.5 kV and cable-charging at or below 24 kV are generally unnecessary ([[iec-56]] 6.111.1). Laboratory verification of [[rated-line-charging-breaking-current]] is valid only if the breaker is restrike-free ([[iec-56]] 6.111.2). Two supply circuits (A and B) are used ([[iec-56]] 6.111.3). Four [[test-duty]] series (Table XIX) at 20-40% and 100% or more of rated capacitive breaking current, with 10 three-phase (or 12 single-phase) tests each ([[iec-56]] 6.111.8). Acceptance requires no restrikes and trapped-charge voltage held 0.3 s ([[iec-56]] 6.111.9).
magnetizing-and-small-inductive-current-: These tests address breaking small inductive currents — transformer magnetizing current, reactor and motor currents — where premature current chopping before natural current zero can excite the load inductance and capacitance into high [[transient-recovery-voltage]] overvoltages. For circuit-breakers rated 100 kV and above, experience shows overvoltages when interrupting unloaded-transformer steady-state magnetizing current at or below rated voltage are small, so no tests are specified; inrush magnetizing current switching is not a normal service condition and is likewise untested ([[iec-56]] 6.112.1). Below 100 kV tests are generally not required, but in cases of doubt should be made on the system under actual service conditions, or three-phase in a laboratory using the actual transformer, the source having as low a capacitance as possible without exceeding the rated TRV ([[iec-56]] 6.112.2). Transformers with reactor-loaded tertiaries, shunt reactors and HV motors are treated as special cases by agreement or are under consideration ([[iec-56]] 6.112.3-6.112.5). Related: [[critical-current-test]], [[restrike]].
